name: IKS Contrition
_comment: R3.39, Module R3 SSD book page 6. Corner reads YS:135 DK:3 EX:8 CR:2; the annex agrees on
crew 14 and 6 boarding parties, both identical to the E4 this is converted from.
POINT VALUE 62/40 is R3.R51's economic/combat split; 40 applies because the crew is poor.
ONE penal difference here, not the usual two: security 2 instead of the E4's 1. There is NO
centerWarp, and that is the point — R3.R53 says the improved catastrophic-damage escape 'does
not apply to the E4J penal escort (R3.39), which does not have a warp-powered boom', and the
sheet bears it out: where the D6J and D5J booms carry WRP-C / IMP / WRP-C, this one carries
an 'E IMP' box and nothing else. The owner called it before the sheet was read — the E4J was
too small for boom separation, so it does not get the extra power.
The annex's 'ISF' note is explained at the foot of the sheet: 'E4Js assigned to the Internal
Security Forces have inferior fire control to those ships in the deep space fleet.' Not
modelled — it is a scenario-assignment property, not a property of the hull.
The annex prints '--' in the HET column for the E4 as well as the E4J, so whatever that means
it is a property of this hull and not of the conversion; bonusHets matches the E4 rather than
inventing a difference the chart does not draw.
_refitComment: B REFIT (Y165) = +3 and Y175 REFIT = +1, both off the ship data table, and the sheet carries
the 'shaded boxes are added by the B refit' legend.
Deliberately NOT carrying over the E4's ADD. The E4's B refit fits an ADD-6, but this sheet
has no ADD box and no anti-drone table at all, so the penal ship's refit converts the rack and
raises the shields and that is all. The same reasoning that wrongly gave the D6J range-30
disruptors says to check this one rather than assume it.
Rack note on the sheet: a type-F rack with one reload; the B refit makes it type-A (FD3.1),
lifting FD3.6's restrictions and the chain-reaction risk; the Y175 refit makes it type-B
